votes.bill: FY2022 final millage resolution (4.2 mills), first motion
votes.what: Motion to approve the resolution adopting the final FY2022 millage rate (the resolution title in the minutes states 4.2 mills, above the 4.1046-mill rolled-back rate).
votes.result: failed (minutes record a 2-1 vote with Burkett and Velasquez in opposition; Kesl and Salzhauer absent)
votes.note: Only three members present. A later motion that day to set the rate at 4.2 carried with a 2-1 vote with Burkett in opposition. Tally wording is quoted as the minutes state it (scanned PDF, OCR text).

votes.bill: FY2022 final millage at 4.3499 mills (as stated in resolution)
votes.what: Motion to adopt the final millage rate as stated in the resolution (4.3499 mills, 5.98% above the rolled-back rate).
votes.result: carried 2-1 (Burkett opposed; Kesl and Salzhauer absent)
votes.note: Minutes record Burkett saying he would not vote to increase the rate. The commission later that night set the rate at 4.2 mills by 3-0 (next entry).

votes.bill: FY2022 final millage set at 4.2 mills
votes.what: Motion to set the final FY2022 millage rate at 4.2 mills (2.32% above the rolled-back rate).
votes.note: Final millage action of the night; Burkett's Yea read from the unanimous 3-0 tally of the three members present. Same meeting also had two earlier 2-1 votes with Burkett opposed on this item.

votes.note: Burkett's Yea read from the unanimous 3-0 tally of three members present.

votes.note: Minutes name Burkett among the two in opposition. Earlier at the same meeting a motion to add the kiosk for reconsideration failed 2-2 with Burkett and Velasquez opposed (Salzhauer absent then).

votes.what: The commission approved the purchase contract and a budget resolution moving $800,000 to the CRA land account.
votes.note: Joiner moved, Williams seconded. Nay: Smith.

votes.bill: Ordinance 2025-13: Juvenile curfew
votes.what: The commission adopted a local juvenile curfew ordinance incorporating Florida Statutes 877.20-877.25.
votes.note: Whitaker moved, Williams seconded. Nay: Smith. Joiner presided as Vice-Mayor (Mayor not present); minutes name only Smith as nay with all five commissioners present, so Joiner's yea is by the minutes' count rather than named.

votes.bill: Ordinance 2026-02: Charter amendment, city boundary map (first reading)
votes.what: The commission approved first reading of the proposed charter amendment adding a city boundary map to go to voters in November 2026.
votes.note: Joiner moved, Whitaker seconded.

votes.bill: Ordinance 2026-02: Charter amendment, city boundary map (adoption for Nov 2026 ballot)
votes.what: The commission adopted the ordinance placing the boundary-map charter amendment on the November 2026 ballot.
votes.note: Cornwell moved, Whitaker seconded. Nay: Smith. Joiner attended by Zoom; minutes name only Smith as nay, so Joiner's yea is by the minutes' count.

votes.bill: Ordinance 2026-03: Charter amendment on term limits (decision not to move forward)
votes.what: The commission voted not to move forward with a proposed charter amendment on term limits for the Mayor and commissioners.
votes.note: Cornwell moved, Joiner seconded the motion to not move forward. Nay: Williams.

votes.bill: Terminate purchase contract for the Tower property ($5,650,000)
votes.what: The commission terminated the city's Feb 19, 2026 contract to buy 710 5th St W, 515 7th St W and 417 7th Ave W from Palmetto Tower TYJ LLC.
votes.note: Cornwell moved, Williams seconded. Joiner was the lone nay.

votes.bill: Proposed FY2027 aggregate millage rate of 5.9671
votes.what: Joiner moved to set the proposed FY2027 millage at 5.9671 and schedule budget hearings; the motion did not pass. A lower proposed rate of 5.8445 was approved 4-1 on Aug 3, 2026 (Williams nay).
votes.note: Joiner moved, Williams seconded. Minutes say it "failed 3-2" but name only Cornwell and Smith as nays, an internal inconsistency; treat the count with caution.

votes.bill: FY2027 final millage (Res 2026-16) and final budget (Res 2026-17)
votes.what: The commission adopted the FY2027 final millage and the FY2027 final budget.
votes.note: Joiner moved both (Whitaker seconded millage; Williams seconded budget). Rate not stated in motion text.

Sunshine Joiner.gaps: Reviewed City of Palmetto commission minutes (docsonline.palmettofl.org) from Sept 2024 through Sept 28, 2026 for split votes and key items; did not open news coverage. Minutes before 2024 list her as "Sunshine Mathews, Ward 2," so no pre-2024 votes are included. Minutes record only the vote count and who dissented, so for "carried 4-1" style items without a roll call, her yea is by the minutes' own count; entries where she moved, seconded or was named as a nay are explicit and are marked as such in notes. Not covered: police/fire specifics, utilities/WWTP privatization votes (Resolution 2026-20 was 5-0 on 2026-09-14 but not itemized here), CRA board votes (separate body), and the July 20, 2026 millage motion is recorded with an internal inconsistency (see note).

votes.bill: 834 Riverside Drive: select Apogee Real Estate Partners as top-ranked developer
votes.what: The commission (acting with the CRA) approved the Riverside Review Committee's top-ranked developer, Apogee Real Estate Partners, and authorized negotiating the sale and development of the property.
votes.note: Jones moved, Williams seconded. Nay: Smith.

votes.bill: Palmetto Sports Complex: proceed to design and ITB/RFP (14th Ave W & 9th St W)
votes.what: The commission approved moving ahead with engineering and construction plans and an ITB/RFP for a sports complex with courts, trail, parking and restrooms, with final design to return to the commission first.
votes.note: Jones moved, Williams seconded. Nay: Smith.

votes.bill: Ordinance 2023-04: Comprehensive Plan text amendments on density/intensity calculation
votes.what: The commission adopted comprehensive plan text amendments clarifying how maximum density and intensity are calculated for future land use categories.
votes.note: Williams moved, Cornwell seconded. Nays: Smith and Jones.

votes.bill: Resolution 2023-18: rescind 1943 resolution on use of property as a cemetery
votes.what: The commission adopted a resolution rescinding an unnamed October 5, 1943 resolution on use of property as a cemetery (pulled from the consent agenda).
votes.note: Williams moved, Cornwell seconded. Nays: Jones and Smith.

votes.bill: Shorten agenda delivery from 10 days to 5 days before meetings
votes.what: The commission voted to have agendas in commissioners' hands 5 days instead of 10 before a meeting.
votes.note: Williams moved, Cornwell seconded. Nays: Jones and Smith. Minutes record Jones saying 10 days gives the commission and public ample time to review. Jones was Vice-Mayor at this meeting.

votes.bill: Ordinance 2023-05: planned development code amendments (Chapters 8, 9, 10)
votes.what: The commission adopted zoning code changes for development plans and planned developments.
votes.note: Joiner moved, Cornwell seconded. Nays: Smith and Jones.

votes.bill: Remove November 4, 2024 meeting from the schedule
votes.what: The commission voted to cancel the November 4, 2024 regular meeting (the day before the general election).
votes.note: Smith moved, Jones seconded. Nay: Williams.

votes.bill: Appoint Rowena Young-Gopie as CRA Director and approve consultant agreement with Edward Johnson
votes.what: The commission appointed a new CRA Director for a term ending January 2025 and approved a consultant agreement keeping the interim director as consultant.
votes.note: Jones made the main motion, Williams seconded. Nays: Smith and Cornwell.

votes.bill: Raise CRA Director salary to match other department heads (secondary motion)
votes.what: Jones moved to adjust the new CRA Director's salary to match other department heads; the motion failed.
votes.note: Jones moved, Smith seconded. Nays: Joiner, Cornwell, Williams.

votes.bill: Unsolicited proposal from Gray Property Group (move forward under s. 255.065)
votes.what: Williams moved to proceed with Gray Property Group's unsolicited proposal; the motion failed. Jones then moved to defer it, which passed 5-0.
votes.note: Nays: Smith, Cornwell, Jones. Jones moved (Cornwell seconded) the follow-up motion to defer, passed 5-0.

votes.bill: Altier purchase agreement (sales contract with Bradford Baker)
votes.what: The commission approved a sales contract with developer Bradford Baker; staff said approval covered the contract only.
votes.note: Nays: Smith and Jones.

votes.bill: FY2025 final millage (Res 2024-23) and final budget (Res 2024-24)
votes.what: The commission adopted the FY2025 final millage and final budget.
votes.note: Unanimous 5-0 with Jones present and listed as Commissioner-at-Large 1.
